title: Remote blood pressure monitoring after hypertensive pregnancy: a pragmatic trial in a regional maternity unit
subtitle: Remote monitoring with midwife-led titration against usual community checks
statement: About 412 women a year leave a regional maternity unit with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, and blood pressure often peaks after discharge when it is checked only around day five and at six weeks. Last year 38 of these women were readmitted with postpartum hypertension. The unit wants to know whether remote monitoring with midwife-led medication titration, delivered by its own midwives, improves blood pressure outcomes compared with usual community checks, without excluding women who lack a smartphone or speak little English.
whoAffected: Women after pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension, their newborns and families, community midwives, the midwife-led hub and the maternity assessment unit.
whatHurts: Uncontrolled blood pressure after birth leads to headaches, readmission, separation from the newborn and, rarely, stroke; women without devices or English may be missed most.
currentPractice: Discharge on day two or three, a midwife check around day five, and a family doctor check at six weeks; medicines adjusted at those contacts only.
whyNow: Charity funding for 300 monitors and an 18-month app licence (HC-2026-017) and an approved titration protocol (MAT-HTN-04) make a trial possible now.
constraints: Charity funding covers 300 monitors and the app licence for 18 months. The midwife hub runs from 08:00 to 20:00; high readings out of hours go to the maternity assessment unit. No extra clinic visits for trial purposes.
patientCenteredGoal: Every woman leaves hospital with a safe way to have her blood pressure watched and treated at home, whatever her phone, language or circumstances.
summary: Problem framed as a pragmatic comparison of remote monitoring with usual postpartum checks.
